basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 46:7 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 268. Quomodo dicitur: Filii ejus et filiae descenderunt cum Jacob in Aegyptum'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 268. Quomodo dicitur: Filii ejus et filiae descenderunt cum Jacob in Aegyptum (Gen. XLVI, 7), cum Jacob plures non habuerit filias, quam Dinam tantummodo?-- Resp. Aut [etiam] neptes filiarum nomine intelligere debemus; aut pluralis numerus pro singulari positus est, sicut ibi: Misit in eis muscam caninam.
